audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1, Level 2 and Level 6 are given to Dr. Mundo or to Skill in both layers, while the whys on those exact rows read 'you lead', 'your early trades win' and 'your burst plus R still out-paces his early R healing'. The packet chart is Garen for the first six stages and Garen wins 55.55% over 3345 games. The full layer is also rated TRICKY 7.5/10 for a lane Garen wins clearly.
audit.why: Three rows contradicted their own text, the packet and the win rate, and the difficulty badge told the reader to fear a lane the data says they dominate.
audit.corrected: Chart proposed as one group: Garen through first item, Dr. Mundo at two items, matching the packet and the mirror's settlement. diff to EVEN, diffRating to 5.5/10, tone to the even colour.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing advice and no ability on this page carries a number. Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15, Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s at every rank, Infected Bonesaw is 4s, Blunt Force Trauma is 9/8.25/7.5/6.75/6.
audit.why: The whole lane is 'leave before the Heart Zapper recast, come back on its downtime', and that instruction is worthless without 17 seconds attached. Maximum Dosage never getting shorter than 120s is the reason his level-6 spike is weaker than it looks.
audit.corrected: Heart Zapper's 17s at rank 1 and the store-then-burst timing written into mid; Maximum Dosage's flat 120s into spikes[1]; Infected Bonesaw's 4s into spikes[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Three real interactions were absent or wrong. (a) Two fields say the Q silence 'stops his cleaver' — Infected Bonesaw is on a 4-second cooldown, so a brief silence barely dents it; what actually matters is that it deals damage based on your CURRENT health, so it hurts most when you are healthy and least when you are not. (b) Heart Zapper stores a portion of damage he takes and heals him when it bursts, so spinning through the full duration is what feeds him. (c) Goes Where He Pleases resists the FIRST immobilizing effect that hits him, which is a jungle-setup fact and appears nowhere.
audit.why: The current-health scaling inverts the usual instinct, the stored-damage mechanic explains why long trades lose, and the passive decides whether a gank lands at all.
audit.corrected: Current-health scaling in spikes[0]; the store-and-burst timing with 'leave before the recast' in mid and early; the first-immobilizing-effect passive written into report[10] as the gank instruction. Blunt Force Trauma named as the auto-reset tell in early. Grievous Wounds moved into wants.you[2] as the anti-heal trigger.

audit.why: Mortal Reminder as a priority third is right against Heart Zapper's damage-stored healing and Maximum Dosage's missing-health heal.

edits.before: Your engage is premium gank setup — ping your jungler when Heart Zapper is down. Ward river before extended trades; you are most gankable mid-combo.
edits.after: Ping your jungler when Heart Zapper is down, and warn him: Mundo's passive resists the FIRST immobilizing effect, so the second piece of CC is the one that lands.

edits.before: Level 1 Mundo has no burst and your Q silence beats his cleaver, so you lead.
edits.after: Level 1 Mundo has no burst and no answer to your step-up, so you lead.

edits.before: You bully early Mundo hard - before he stacks HP your Q silence stops his cleaver and your E shreds his low-armor early body while his passive regen can't keep pace.
edits.after: You bully early Mundo — Infected Bonesaw is a 4s poke that scales off your CURRENT health, so it hurts most when you are full. Spin his low-armour body and leave.

edits.before: You still lead: your burst plus R chunk out-paces his R Maximum Dosage healing before he has the HP pool to abuse it.
edits.after: You still lead: Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s at every rank, so force it out early and take the fight in the two minutes after.

edits.before: You win outright. Early Mundo is a slow, low-armor target with no burst - lead with Q to silence his cleaver, spin E inside the wave, and his passive regen can't offset your trades. Punish every cleaver he throws and deny him CS to choke his HP scaling before it starts.
edits.after: You win outright. Early Mundo is slow and low-armour with no burst - trade on his last-hits and leave before Heart Zapper bursts. Blunt Force Trauma is an auto reset, so the wind-up is your cue to step back, not the cast. Deny him CS to choke his HP scaling before it starts.

edits.before: Stay on top through 6. Your damage and R chunk out-pace his healing while his HP pool is still small, so keep trading and looking for kills. Every time you deny a wave or force a back, you delay the moment his sustain becomes a problem - press the tempo you built early.
edits.after: Stay on top through 6. Heart Zapper stores a share of the damage you deal and heals him when it bursts - 17s at rank 1 - so break off before the recast lands and step back in on its downtime. Every wave you deny delays the moment his sustain becomes a problem.

edits.before: Silence his Q cleaver and deny CS in the early levels
edits.after: Deny CS early: his entire game plan is the health bar

edits.before: Kill him before his HP and R healing come online
edits.after: Buy Grievous Wounds before Heart Zapper is ranked up

notes: The highest-value fact added here is on the jungle line: Goes Where He Pleases resists the first immobilizing effect that hits him and drops a cannister he can pick up to heal. Garen's own kit has no immobilize, so this only ever matters for a gank — and it was nowhere on the page. Also corrected a piece of advice that would waste the silence: Infected Bonesaw is a 4-second ability, so 'silence his cleaver' is not a plan; its current-health scaling is the thing worth knowing. The missing-interactions feed lists Maximum Dosage under 'resistances-invalidated', but Riot's text for it is purely a heal plus move speed and regeneration — the percentHealth flag is about healing, not damage, so I did not write any resistance-bypass claim from it.
